title: payment-api degradation runbook
body: When payment-api reports degraded: 1) check dependency dashboard checkout-db and payment-gateway; 2) if error rate > 5%, create a high severity incident; 3) roll back the last deployment if the degradation started within 30 minutes of a release; 4) notify the payments on-call.

title: Incident severity matrix
body: severity low: cosmetic or single user impact. medium: single service degraded with a workaround. high: customer-facing impact or revenue path affected. critical: full outage of a revenue path or data integrity risk.

title: On-call escalation guide
body: Primary on-call handles first response within 15 minutes. If not acknowledged, escalate to secondary, then to the service owner. Always link the incident ticket in the team channel.

title: checkout-service troubleshooting
body: checkout-service slowness is usually caused by downstream payment-api latency or redis cache misses. Verify payment-api status first, then check redis memory and hit rate.

title: Deployment rollback procedure
body: Use the deployment console, select the service, click Rollback to previous revision. Rollbacks take 3-5 minutes. Always create an incident before rolling back a revenue-path service.

title: Database failover runbook
body: If checkout-db fails over, verify replication lag before reopening writes. Expected failover time is under 90 seconds. Check the events table for the failover trigger.

title: Notification service rate limits
body: notification-service allows 1000 messages per minute per template. Exceeding the limit returns 429 and messages are queued, not lost. Backpressure resolves within 2 minutes.

title: auth-service token rotation
body: auth-service rotates signing keys every 24 hours. Clients cache old keys for up to 1 hour, so brief 401 spikes after rotation are expected and self-heal.

title: Monitoring and alerts overview
body: Golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation. Alert routing: page for critical, email for high, dashboard-only for medium and low. Alert silence windows must be approved by the service owner.

title: POST /v1/payments API reference
body: POST /v1/payments charges a payment intent. 402 means the card was declined by the issuer. 503 means the gateway is unavailable; retry with idempotency-key. Sustained 5xx requires an incident.

title: search-service indexing lag
body: search-service indexing lag over 5 minutes indicates the indexer queue is backed up. Restart the indexer pod, then verify lag returns under 1 minute. Do not reindex the full corpus.

title: PII handling in incidents
body: Never include customer PII (emails, card numbers, addresses) in incident titles or descriptions. Reference customer IDs instead. The incident system is readable by all engineering staff.
